title: Piano Movers in Glendale | SOS Moving
metaDescription: Glendale piano movers from SOS: an hourly crew of four, a $200 instrument add-on, piano board, straps and door padding. Booking daily, 8AM to 6PM.
heroSubtitle: Four movers, a board and straps — your instrument travels inside the same hourly job as the rest of the furniture.

faq.question: Our house sits above the street with an outdoor stair. Is that still an ordinary hourly job?
faq.answer: Yes. Outdoor steps change the pace rather than the billing — four movers still work by the hour with the $200 instrument add-on on top. Send a photo of the flight when you book so the lead can mark the pause points in advance.

faq.question: Do piano movers in Glendale need a gate pass for Chevy Chase Canyon?
faq.answer: There is nothing to apply for. The Chevy Chase Estates Association keeps membership optional and imposes no CC&Rs or resident regulations, and the windshield decal it hands out identifies residents rather than contractors. We confirm the canyon road is open before the truck leaves.

faq.question: Is the instrument invoiced on its own?
faq.answer: No. It is a $200 add-on inside an hourly move, which is why it only runs with a crew of four. There is no separate instrument price list and no per-mile rate for a piano.

faq.question: Can you come on the same day I call?
faq.answer: Often, yes. It depends on a four-person crew being free, and the office answers on 909-443-0004 from 8AM to 6PM every day of the week. A morning call gives the dispatcher room to fit the job in.

faq.question: Will you tune or value the instrument afterwards?
faq.answer: The crew carries the instrument in and places it on the spot you point to, and that is where our part ends. Tuning, appraisal, disposal and instrument storage sit outside what SOS does, so most owners book a technician a couple of weeks later, once the piano has settled into its new room.

faq.question: What should be ready before the crew arrives?
faq.answer: Clear the carry route, roll back rugs, take door stops out of the way and free the curb in front of the entrance. If the building wants a certificate of insurance, say so a day ahead — it costs $50 and has to exist before arrival.
